title: Consistency vs Availability
subtitle: PACELC theorem, quorum intersection math, session guarantees, and bounded staleness.
keyTakeaways: The CAP theorem only applies during rare network partitions; the PACELC theorem captures normal operations: if there is a Partition, choose Availability or Consistency; Else, choose Latency or Consistency.

Strong consistency does not have to be an all-or-nothing choice across the entire system: use linearizable quorums for financial balances, and session-consistent or eventual models for user feeds and search catalogs.

Enforce "read-your-writes" consistency at low latency by returning the database Write-Ahead Log Log Sequence Number (LSN) to the client, routing read queries to replicas that have caught up to that specific LSN.

sections.heading: PACELC Theorem and Quorum Intersection Mechanics
sections.body: The traditional CAP theorem states that under a network partition (P), a distributed system must choose between Consistency (C) and Availability (A). However, partitions are rare events in well-engineered data centers. Daniel Abadi's PACELC theorem expands CAP to describe normal day-to-day operations: If Partition (P), trade Availability (A) vs Consistency (C); Else (E), trade Latency (L) vs Consistency (C).
bullets: The latency trade-off during normal operations: Even when networks are 100% healthy, demanding linearizable reads requires coordinating across multiple nodes (paying network round-trip latency). Opting for low-latency local reads means accepting the possibility of reading stale data.

Strict quorum intersection formula: In a cluster of N replicas, strict consistency is guaranteed if Read Quorum (R) + Write Quorum (W) > N. For a 5-node cluster, setting W=3 and R=3 ensures that any read quorum intersects with at least one replica holding the latest write.

Sloppy quorums and hinted handoff: Systems like DynamoDB or Cassandra can fall back to sloppy quorums during outages, writing temporary hints to non-designated nodes to maintain availability at the cost of immediate consistency.

codeSnippet.title: Session-Consistent Read-Your-Writes Routing via LSN High-Water Mark

sections.heading: Client-Centric Consistency and Session Guarantees
sections.body: Full linearizability across all operations is expensive and unnecessary for most user experiences. Client-centric consistency models provide targeted guarantees that eliminate user-visible anomalies without paying the cost of global two-phase commit.
bullets: Read-your-writes consistency: A user submits a post, refreshes their profile page, and sees their new post immediately. It does not matter if other users see the post 500ms later, as long as the author never sees their own submission disappear.

Implementing read-your-writes via LSN tokens: When the primary database commits a write, it returns the current Log Sequence Number (LSN) or version token in the response. The client passes this token on subsequent read requests; the read router directs the query to a replica that has caught up to that LSN, or falls back to the primary.

Monotonic read guarantees: Guarantees that if a user observes a particular state, they will never subsequently observe an older state on subsequent queries (preventing "time-travel" anomalies when reading from lagging replicas).

tradeOffs.pros: Zero data staleness; operations behave as if executed sequentially on a single machine; no dirty reads.
tradeOffs.cons: Every write and strong read incurs cross-node network latency; write availability halts if a partition breaks quorum.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Financial ledgers, seat reservation inventories, and cluster leader election state.

tradeOffs.pros: Eliminates jarring user-facing staleness while allowing 95%+ of read traffic to hit cheap, horizontally scaled replicas.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires routing logic to track client replication tokens and handle fallback paths if replicas lag.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Social media profile updates, e-commerce reviews, and collaborative document editing.

interviewTip: Do not simply say "I choose eventual consistency for high availability." Show deeper seniority by specifying session consistency guarantees: explain how passing an LSN high-water mark token in client requests guarantees read-your-writes consistency without routing all traffic to the primary database.
